findings.claim: The OpenCode plugin-load check reads the project path from process.argv[2], but `node --input-type=module - "$opencode_project"` (script from stdin) places the first user argument at process.argv[1], so argv[2] is undefined and `path.join(undefined, ...)` throws — the gate can never pass and the new CI job is permanently red.
findings.evidence: Hunk: `node --input-type=module - "$opencode_project" <<'NODE'` followed by `const project = process.argv[2]`. For stdin/`-e` scripts Node omits the script-path slot, so argv is [execPath, "$opencode_project"]. The same script's own `manifest_harness_version` correctly uses `process.argv[1]` for the same invocation pattern, proving the off-by-one.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to `process.argv[2] ?? process.argv[1]` validation or, concretely, use `const project = process.argv[1]` and assert it is defined before path.join.

findings.claim: Task 1.1 requires 'bounded redacted logs', but the script implements no log capture, bounding, or redaction whatsoever — harness output is either discarded to /dev/null (destroying failure diagnostics under set -e) or streamed raw and unbounded to the CI log.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 1.1: 'lifecycle qualification with named-version enforcement and bounded redacted logs'. The script contains no log file, no size cap, no redaction pass; e.g. `CODEX_HOME=... "$codex_binary" plugin marketplace add ... --json >/dev/null` and unredirected stderr from every harness invocation.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture each stage's output to a bounded file (e.g. head -c N), apply a redaction filter for tokens/paths, and emit the redacted excerpt only on failure.

findings.claim: The 'upgrade' stages reinstall the byte-identical artifact (Codex re-runs `plugin add` on the same marketplace package; OpenCode runs `npm install --force` of the same tarball), so file-replacement/stale-file semantics of a real version-to-version upgrade are never exercised.
findings.evidence: Hunk comment 'Codex documents plugin add as the reinstall/update operation' followed by repeating the identical `plugin add compass@compass-plugins`; `npm install --ignore-scripts --force --prefix "$opencode_project" "$scratch/$tarball"` reuses the same tarball packed moments earlier. Criterion 1.2 requires upgrade coverage of the lifecycle.
findings.suggested_fix: Export a second, modified package (or bump a content file) and upgrade from artifact A to artifact B, then assert B's content is what the harness serves.

findings.claim: Criterion 1.2's 'complete skill discovery, MCP configuration/load' is not verified for Codex or Claude: the script only greps `plugin list`/`mcp list` output, which matches registered config entries without proving the harness discovered skills or completed an MCP handshake with the compass server.
findings.evidence: `CODEX_HOME=... "$codex_binary" mcp list | grep -q 'compass'` and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=... "$claude_binary" mcp list | grep -q 'compass'` — listing registered servers is configuration presence, not load; a stale or broken entry that fails to spawn would still grep-match. Only the OpenCode plugin is actually executed (via direct node import, not via the harness).
findings.suggested_fix: Drive an actual MCP initialize/tools-list round trip against the registered server per harness, and assert the harness reports the umbrella/focused skills as discovered.

findings.claim: The user-sentinel preservation scenario proves nothing for Codex: HOME is never redirected for codex commands (only CODEX_HOME), and the sentinel at $state/user is outside Codex's managed state, so a Codex install/upgrade/uninstall that clobbered user files beside its real state would go undetected.
findings.evidence: Sentinel is `$state/user/USER-INSTRUCTIONS.md`; claude/opencode invocations set `HOME="$state/user"`, but all codex invocations set only `CODEX_HOME="$codex_home"`. Spec scenario: 'a sentinel instruction exists beside managed harness state … install, upgrade, and uninstall SHALL preserve its bytes' — for Codex the sentinel is not beside any state the harness touches.
findings.suggested_fix: Place a sentinel inside/adjacent to CODEX_HOME-managed territory (and run codex with an isolated HOME) so the preservation assertion binds to each harness's lifecycle.

findings.claim: `export PATH="$(dirname "$compass_binary"):$PATH"` exports a relative PATH entry (`target/debug` given the CI invocation `--compass target/debug/compass`), so any PATH-based `compass` resolution by a harness breaks after the script's `cd "$opencode_project"`.
findings.evidence: CI hunk: `scripts/qualify_harness_packages.sh --compass target/debug/compass`; script line 62 exports dirname verbatim; line 129 changes cwd inside a subshell that then invokes the opencode harness whose MCP configuration may spawn `compass` from PATH.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve to an absolute path first, e.g. `compass_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "$compass_binary")" && pwd)"; export PATH="$compass_dir:$PATH"`.

findings.claim: CI no longer runs the existing unit/library/binary test suites anywhere: `--lib --bins` runs were deleted from both the quality and cross-target matrix jobs, and `cargo test --workspace --test '*'` skips doctests, so previously-green unit and doc tests can silently rot.
findings.evidence: Removed lines: `cargo test --workspace --lib --bins --locked` (quality), `cargo nextest run --workspace --lib --bins --locked`, and `cargo test --workspace --lib --bins --locked --target ${{ matrix.target }}`; replacements select only `--test '*'`, which excludes lib tests, bin tests, and doctests. The constraints prohibit unit tests as *new evidence* but do not direct removing existing coverage from CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a `--lib --bins` (and doctests, if any) leg in CI alongside the new integration-target runs, or document the deliberate removal in the change.

findings.claim: `cargo nextest run --workspace --test '*' --locked` relies on cargo-style glob target selection that nextest does not necessarily implement; if unsupported or zero-matching, the isolation gate either errors out or silently runs no tests while passing.
findings.evidence: Hunk: `- run: cargo nextest run --workspace --test '*' --locked`. The prior line used `--lib --bins`, which nextest documents; glob patterns in `--test` are a cargo target-selection feature and are not a documented nextest target-selection behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Use nextest's supported selection (e.g. `cargo nextest run --workspace --tests` or a filterset expression) and verify locally that the command enumerates the intended integration targets.

findings.claim: Task 2.1 requires wiring 'the lifecycle and OpenCode JavaScript integration gates into CI', but the new installed-agent-packages job runs only `npm ci` — no `npm run typecheck:js` or `npm run test:js` step appears anywhere in the diff.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 2.1; new job steps end at `Qualify installed native packages` with no JS typecheck/test step; constraint js-surface-verified (`npm ci && npm run typecheck:js && npm run test:js`) applies to the OpenCode plugin surface this change exercises.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `npm run typecheck:js` and `npm run test:js` steps to the new job (or cite the existing job that covers them in the change record).

findings.claim: Every `harness … | grep -q …` runs under `set -o pipefail`; grep -q exits immediately on first match, so a harness that keeps writing receives SIGPIPE (exit 141) and the pipeline fails spuriously for large outputs, making the gate flaky.
findings.evidence: `set -euo pipefail` at line 2 combined with e.g. `"$codex_binary" plugin list --available --json | grep -q '"compass"'` and `"$opencode_binary" mcp list` piped to `grep -q 'compass'`.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture output into a bounded variable/file first, then grep the capture (which also enables the required log bounding).

findings.claim: The globally installed harness packages are version-pinned but not integrity-pinned, and the version-equality checks in the script parse `--version` output with inconsistent, format-fragile awk fields that fail silently via bare `[[ ]]` with no diagnostic message.
findings.evidence: Workflow: `npm install --global @openai/codex@0.146.0 @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.251 opencode-ai@1.18.23` (no lockfile/integrity, unlike the SHA-pinned actions in the same file). Script: `awk '{print $NF}'` for codex/opencode vs `awk '{print $1}'` for claude, then bare `[[ "$actual_codex_version" == "$expected_codex_version" ]]` which exits 1 with no output on mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Install via a lockfile-controlled `npm ci` (or record integrity), and emit an echo of expected-vs-actual before each comparison.

findings.claim: The harness binary variables are expanded unquoted in command substitutions (`$($codex_binary --version …)` etc.), so an override path containing spaces passed via --codex/--claude/--opencode silently mis-parses.
findings.evidence: `actual_codex_version="$($codex_binary --version | awk '{print $NF}')"` and the analogous claude/opencode lines, despite the script accepting arbitrary paths for these options.
